Ivy C: Hey all - first week snag. Switched to Colima and my postgres in docker-compose exits with "could not write lock file "/var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid": Permission denied". I have the data dir as a host bind mount and also mounted /var/run/docker.sock into a helper container. Any quick tips?

Marcus G: welcome! socket mount itself shouldn't change PG data perms. On mac Colima host mounts often appear owned by root inside the VM. Best is to use a named volume for PG or chown the host dir from inside the colima VM to uid 999.

Marcus G: ```bash
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /path/to/pgdata
exit
docker-compose up -d db
```

Hannah: FWIW mounting docker.sock into dev containers can cause files created by that container to be owned by root on the host volume (if the container talks to the docker daemon as root). Avoid that for day-to-day dev unless you really need it.

Marcus G: Also check you don't have local postgres running on the host (brew services) that might have created files or claimed ports. If you must use host postgres stop the service or map to a nonstandard host port (eg 55432:5432).

Ivy C: Chowned inside colima and pg starts now, thanks. Follow-up: my app sometimes gets ERR NOAUTH when talking to redis even though REDIS_PASSWORD is set in compose. Running redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" inside the container returns PONG.

Hannah: most likely your app is hitting a different Redis (old container or host redis). Run `docker ps` and `ss -ltnp` / `lsof -i :6379` on host. On mac, brew's redis listens on 6379 by default.

Ivy C: Ah yep `brew services list` showed redis started. Stopped it and now app connects to compose redis with auth fine. Also removed docker.sock mount from my helper container while debugging.

ops-bot: dev-runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup  sections: "Colima and host mounts", "Port conflicts and brew services", and "Caution: mounting docker.sock".

Hannah: Nice. Short checklist: 1) prefer named volumes for PG, 2) chown inside colima if using host mounts, 3) avoid docker.sock mounts in dev, 4) stop system services (brew) that conflict, 5) map host ports if you need host tooling.

Ivy C: Thanks everyone! I'll add a quick note to the runbook about brew redis and docker.sock. Appreciate the help :tada:
